Subject: Questions on MSA redline: output ownership & model training

Hi Sean (and Procurement team),

Thanks for sending the draft MSA and order form. We reviewed the redlines and have two primary concerns from a product / legal perspective before procurement will sign: 

1) Output ownership: Section 7.2 in the redline appears to assign broad rights to Redwood over "outputs" derived from customer prompts. We need confirmation that OrbitSoft retains exclusive rights to customer data and any productized output that is a direct transformation of our proprietary datasets.

2) Training / feedback license: The draft includes a perpetual feedback license (Section 9) that would allow using customer data/outputs for model improvement. We can consider a scoped, time-boxed license restricted to non-production telemetry and explicit opt-in.

I've attached the annotated MSA redline (OrbitSoft_MSA_redline_v3.docx) and a short SOC2 evidence packet procurement asked for. Can you confirm Redwood's stance and provide proposed alternative wording for the ownership clause and a limited feedback license? Procurement needs that language to continue.

Thanks,

OrbitSoft

Folks — quick internal note after Elena's message. Key points for negotiation: 
- OrbitSoft is sensitive about any language that could be read as assigning title to outputs that are direct derivatives of their datasets. We should avoid "assignment" language and use "limited license" where necessary.
- For the training/use of telemetry: propose a two-track approach 
  * Track A (default): Redwood may use anonymized, aggregated telemetry for improving the hosted service (model ops, infrastructure) with no commercial transfer rights.
  * Track B (optional): Customer may opt-in to a scoped model improvement program where Redwood can use non-sensitive customer examples for model tuning; opt-in requires explicit checkbox in the order form and a ~12-month sunset.
- Evidence/procurement asks: they want SOC2 artifacts (we provided) and an explanation of data flows (redwood hosted vs dedicated). Laura: can you confirm if any operational changes are required for Track B?

Irene: if you can draft two short redlines (one for Section 7: Outputs and one for Section 9: Feedback/Training) Ican send to Elena with a covering note. Suggested placeholder language for the outputs clause (to iterate):

"Customer retains title to Customer Data and any Output that is a direct transformation of Customer Data. Redwood is granted a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Aggregated and De-identified Output solely to provide and operate the Services."

I'll keep the email to Elena concise.

-Ben

Elena — thanks for the note and redlines. Attached is a tracked-change excerpt with two concise replacements for the flagged sections; Ihave kept your protections front-and-center and added operational guardrails. Summary below and pasted language follows.

Summary: 
- Output ownership: we replaced assignment language with explicit retention by Customer for "Customer Data" and "Direct Outputs" (defined in the clause). Redwood receives a limited license to use only Aggregated or De-identified Outputs for service improvement and diagnostics.
- Training/Feedback: Redwood will not use Customer Data or Direct Outputs for model training unless Customer opts in via the Order Form. Opt-in grants Redwood a time-limited (12 month) non-exclusive license limited to specified datasets and excludes any material marked as "restricted" in the carve-out schedule.

Pasted proposed replacements (for immediate review):

--- Section 7 (Outputs) ---
"Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Data and Direct Outputs (i.e., outputs that are a literal or near-literal transformation of Customer Data). Redwood is granted a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Aggregated or De-identified Outputs solely to operate, secure, and improve the Services; such use shall not include assignment or transfer of Customerownership rights."

--- Section 9 (Feedback & Training) ---
"Redwood shall not use Customer Data or Direct Outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve models used to provide services to third parties without Customer's prior written consent. Customer may, at its election in the Order Form, grant a limited, revocable license to Redwood to use specified data for model improvement for a period not to exceed twelve (12) months from the effective date specified in the Order Form. The parties shall document any dataset-level carve-outs in Schedule A (Carve-Outs)."

Next steps: if that language is acceptable, Sean/Bob (procurement) — sorry cc didn't include Bob earlier, Elena please confirm procurement contact — can we get a short note from you that the language addresses their procurement risk? If OrbitSoft wants a shorter sunset or different exclusions, call them out now and we'll iterate.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
